questions.question: The calendar for the year 2011 will be the same as which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The given year is 2011, which is an Ordinary Year.

We need to count the odd days starting from 2011 until the sum is a multiple of 7:

__
 
• 2011: 1 odd day
 
• 2012: 2 odd days (Leap Year)
 
• 2013: 1 odd day
 
• 2014: 1 odd day
 
• 2015: 1 odd day
 
• 2016: 2 odd days (Leap Year)
 
• 2017: 1 odd day
 
• 2018: 1 odd day
 
• 2019: 1 odd day
 
• 2020: 2 odd days (Leap Year)
 
• 2021: 1 odd day

Sum of odd days = 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 14 odd days.

Since 14 is divisible by 7 (14 ÷ 7 = 2, with 0 remainder), the next year, 2022, will have the same calendar as 2011.

Both 2011 and 2022 are Ordinary Years, so the calendars are identical.

The calendar for the year 2011 will be the same as 2022.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **Alternate Method__****
There is a specific pattern for the repetition of calendars:

 
• If the year is Leap year + 1, the calendar repeats after 6 years.
 
• If the year is Leap year + 2, the calendar repeats after 11 years.
 
• If the year is Leap year + 3, the calendar repeats after 11 years.
 
• If the year is a Leap year, the calendar repeats after 28 years.

The year 2011 follows the Leap year + 3 rule (as 2008 was a Leap year):

2011 = 2008 + 3

Repetition interval = 11 years.

Repeating year = 2011 + 11 = 2022.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 4**”.

questions.question: A clock is 6 minutes slow at 2:20 PM and 12 minutes slow at 8:20 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
questions.solution:
Time interval from 2:20 PM to 8:20 PM = 6 hours.

Initial error at 2:20 PM = 6 minutes slow.

Final error at 8:20 PM = 12 minutes slow.

Total time lost during this interval = 12 minutes − 6 minutes = 6 minutes.

Rate of losing time = 6 minutes ÷ 6 hours = 1 minute per hour.

Time taken to lose 6 minutes = 6 minutes ÷ 1 minute/hour = 6 hours.

Correct time = 2:20 PM − 6 hours = 8:20 AM.

Hence, the clock shows the correct time at 8:20 AM.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: The Council of Ministers in a state is collectively responsible to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The governance of Indian states follows the **Parliamentary system**, where the executive is drawn from and remains accountable to the legislature.
 
• According to **Article 164(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the Council of Ministers shall be **collectively responsible** to the **Legislative Assembly** of the State.
 
• The term **collective responsibility** implies that the entire ministry is viewed as a single unit; they share joint responsibility for all decisions made by the **Cabinet**.
 
• If the **State Legislative Assembly** passes a **No-Confidence Motion** against the government, all ministers, including those belonging to the **Legislative Council** (in bicameral states), must resign collectively.
 
• This mechanism ensures that the **Council of Ministers** retains power only as long as it commands the majority support of the **elected representatives** of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Entities:**

 
 
• **Governor:** While the ministers are collectively responsible to the legislature, they hold office during the **pleasure of the Governor** under **Article 164(1)**, which represents their **individual responsibility**.
 
• **President:** The **President of India** is the constitutional head of the Union; state ministers do not have a direct line of responsibility to the President, though the Governor is appointed by the President.
 
• **Supreme Court:** The **Judiciary** acts as the guardian of the Constitution and can perform **Judicial Review** of executive actions, but the Council of Ministers is not politically responsible to the court.
 
• **State Legislature:** In many states, this includes both the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha) and the **Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad), though collective responsibility specifically targets the **Lower House**.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the joint sitting of Parliament provided?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 108**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 108** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **President** to summon a **joint sitting** of both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** to resolve a legislative deadlock.
 
• A deadlock occurs if a bill is rejected by the other House, if the Houses disagree on **amendments**, or if the second House remains silent for more than **six months**.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over the joint sitting. In the Speaker's absence, the **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha or the **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha takes the chair.
 
• The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (the Vice-President) does not preside over a joint sitting because they are not a member of either House of **Parliament**.
 
• Decisions in a joint sitting are taken by a **simple majority** of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
 
• This provision is applicable only to **Ordinary Bills** and **Financial Bills**, and it cannot be invoked for **Money Bills** or **Constitutional Amendment Bills**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 107**: Deals with the **introduction and passing of Bills**, specifying that except for Money and Financial Bills, a bill may originate in either House.
 
• **Article 109**: Details the **special procedure** for **Money Bills**, clarifying that they cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha and must be returned within **14 days**.
 
• **Article 110**: Provides the **definition of Money Bills**, which includes matters related to **taxation**, public expenditure, and the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
 
 
• The **Speaker's certificate** is required to endorse a bill as a Money Bill, and this decision is **final** and cannot be challenged in court or Parliament.

questions.question: What is the main medium of transmission in Indian folk and tribal music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oral tradition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oral tradition** is the fundamental medium for transmitting **Indian folk and tribal music**, where musical knowledge is inherited through **auditory learning** and **mimicry** rather than formal scripts or notation.
 
• This tradition relies on **collective memory**, allowing the **lyrics**, **melodies**, and **rhythms** to be passed down during **festivals**, **harvests**, and **lifecycle rituals** within communities like the **Bhils**, **Santhals**, and **Munda** tribes.
 
• It serves as a living archive for **regional dialects**, **indigenous folklore**, and **mythological narratives**, ensuring that the **cultural identity** of a group is preserved across centuries without the need for literacy.
 
• The flexibility of this medium allows for **spontaneous improvisation** and the evolution of styles, which is why folk forms like the **Baul** of Bengal or **Pandavani** of Chhattisgarh maintain a dynamic and organic character.
 
• In the absence of **written records**, the **oral medium** ensures that even the most complex **polyrhythmic structures** and **microtonal variations** are mastered by younger members through continuous **participation** in social gatherings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru-Shishya tradition**:

 
 
• This is a formal **pedagogical system** predominantly found in **Indian Classical Music** (both **Hindustani** and **Carnatic**).
 
• It involves a dedicated relationship where a disciple (shishya) lives with the teacher (guru) to master the intricacies of **Ragas**, **Talas**, and specific **Gharana** lineages.
 
 
 
• **Written notation**:
 
 
• While systems like the **Bhatkhande** and **Paluskar** notations were developed in the **20th century** to document classical compositions, they are rarely used in **tribal music**.
 
• The **unscripted nature** of folk music is what distinguishes it from **academic** or **Margi Sangeet**.
 
 
 
• **Audio recordings**:
 
 
• These are modern **technological tools** utilized by organizations like the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** and **ethnomusicologists** for **archival purposes**.
 
• While they help in the **preservation** of endangered art forms, they are not the **traditional primary medium** for the pedagogical transmission of folk music within indigenous communities.

questions.question: The rolling of thunder is mainly due to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Successive reflections of sound**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Thunder is the sound produced by the **rapid expansion** and contraction of air surrounding a path of **lightning**, which heats the air to approximately **30,000 Kelvin**.
 
• The **rolling effect** or rumbling of thunder is primarily caused by the **successive reflections** of sound waves from various surfaces such as **clouds**, **mountains**, and different **layers of air** with varying densities.
 
• Since a lightning bolt can be several kilometers long, sound waves originate from different points along the bolt; these waves reach an observer at different times due to the distance variations and the **echoes** created by **multiple reflections**.
 
• The **acoustic energy** bounces between the **ground and clouds**, or between different cloud formations, preventing the sound from being a single sharp crack and turning it into a prolonged **rumble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resonance of clouds**:

 
 
• Resonance involves a system vibrating at its **natural frequency**. Clouds are composed of water droplets and ice and do not possess the **structural rigidity** required to resonate and produce the rolling sound of thunder.
 
 
 
• **Interference of sound waves**:
 
 
• While **constructive and destructive interference** can occur when sound waves meet, it typically results in variations in **loudness** or intensity rather than the sustained, multi-second duration characteristic of a **thunder roll**.
 
 
 
• **Lightning effect**:
 
 
• Lightning is the **source** of the sound (the cause of the shockwave), but the term 'lightning effect' is too broad and does not specifically explain the **temporal prolongation** and reflection mechanism that creates the rolling sensation.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound vs. Light**:
 
 
• Light travels at approximately **3 x 10⁸ meters per second**, while sound travels at roughly **340 meters per second**. This discrepancy explains why **lightning** is seen almost instantly, while **thunder** is heard later.

questions.question: The Aravalli Range extends from which direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northeast to Southwest**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is one of the oldest **fold mountain systems** in the world, having its origins in the **Proterozoic Era**.
 
• The range extends for approximately **692 kilometers** (430 miles), stretching from **Delhi** in the northeast, passing through **Southern Haryana** and **Rajasthan**, and ending at **Palanpur** in **Gujarat** in the southwest.
 
• The orientation of the range is **Northeast to Southwest**, a position that makes it nearly parallel to the direction of the **Southwest Monsoon** winds, leading to lower rainfall in the **Thar Desert** region.
 
• It serves as a major **geographical divide**, separating the semi-arid **Marwar** region from the more fertile **Mewar** region in Rajasthan.
 
• The range acts as a barrier to the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert**, protecting the fertile **Indo-Gangetic plains** from wind erosion and sand deposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Shikhar**:

 
 
• Located in the **Mount Abu** hills, it is the highest peak of the **Aravalli Range** with an elevation of **1,722 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrology and Rivers**:
 
 
• Several important rivers originate or are fed by the Aravallis, including the **Luni River** (which flows into the Rann of Kutch), the **Sabarmati**, and the **Banas River**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance**:
 
 
• The range is exceptionally rich in mineral resources, providing significant deposits of **copper**, **zinc**, **lead**, **silver**, and construction materials like **Makrana marble**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Role**:
 
 
• It functions as a **wildlife corridor** and contains several protected areas, such as the **Sariska Tiger Reserve** and the **Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary**.

questions.question: Which economist gave the concept of comparative advantage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ricardo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Ricardo**, a prominent 19th-century British political economist, first formulated the **Theory of Comparative Advantage** in his seminal work, **On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation**, published in **1817**.
 
• The concept explains that international trade can be mutually beneficial even if one nation has an **absolute advantage** in producing every single good; the key lies in **relative efficiency** and **opportunity cost**.
 
• **Opportunity cost** refers to the value of the next best alternative foregone; **Ricardo** argued that countries should specialize in producing goods where their **opportunity cost** is the lowest compared to other nations.
 
• He famously illustrated this using the example of **England and Portugal** producing **cloth and wine**, demonstrating that total global output increases when each nation focuses on its **comparative strength**.
 
• This theory remains a cornerstone of **classical international trade theory** and provides the fundamental logical justification for **free trade** policies globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adam Smith**:

 
 
• Known as the **Father of Modern Economics**, he authored **The Wealth of Nations** in **1776**.
 
• He introduced the **Theory of Absolute Advantage**, suggesting that a country should specialize in goods it can produce more efficiently than any other.
 
 
 
• **John Maynard Keynes**:
 
 
• A 20th-century economist who founded **Keynesian Economics** and wrote **The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money** (1936).
 
• His work focused on **macroeconomic management**, **aggregate demand**, and the role of **government intervention** during economic recessions.
 
 
 
• **John Hicks**:
 
 
• An influential British economist known for his contributions to **general equilibrium theory** and **welfare economics**.
 
• He developed the **IS-LM model**, which serves as a graphical representation of **Keynesian macroeconomic theory**.

Identify **a = 2.5** and **b = 0.5** from the terms.

Direct calculation: **(2.5 − 0.5)³ = (2)³**.

⇒ Substituting these values into the given expression:

⇒ **a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³**

Standard Algebraic Cubic Identities

Difference and Sum of Cubes

Number of terms (n) = 30

Sum of Cubes of First n Natural Numbers

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 52 cm. One of the diagonal is 24 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the other diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of **rhombus** = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

Half of the given diagonal = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Using **Pythagorean Triplet** (5, 12, 13), half of the other diagonal must be 5 cm.

Length of the other **diagonal** = 5 × 2 = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** = 52 cm, One **diagonal** (d₁) = 24 cm.

**Formula Used:** Side² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b9aef6292bbce4b3a89f267b467b7f6366b7064dde81cbebc2da243a2138264.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Side** = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

⇒ Let the other diagonal be d₂.

⇒ (13)² = (24 ÷ 2)² + (d₂ ÷ 2)²

⇒ 169 = (12)² + (d₂ ÷ 2)²

⇒ 169 = 144 + (d₂ ÷ 2)²

⇒ (d₂ ÷ 2)² = 169 − 144 = 25

⇒ d₂ ÷ 2 = √25 = 5

⇒ d₂ = 5 × 2 = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

The area of a **rhombus** can be calculated as Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the **diagonals**.

Properties of Diagonals

The **diagonals** of a rhombus bisect each other at **right angles** (90°), forming four congruent right-angled triangles.

Side-Diagonal Relationship

A direct relationship between **side** (a) and diagonals is given by 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

questions.question: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 46 cm. Side of the rhombus is 17 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relation: (d₁ + d₂)² = 4a² + 4 × Area

Given d₁ + d₂ = 46 cm and side a = 17 cm

⇒ 46² = 4 × 17² + 4 × Area

⇒ 2116 = 1156 + 4 × Area

⇒ 4 × Area = 960 ⇒ Area = 240 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 240 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **diagonals** (d₁ + d₂) = 46 cm

**Side** of the **rhombus** (a) = 17 cm

**Formula Used:**

1) 4a² = d₁² + d₂² (Relation between side and diagonals)

2) Area of **rhombus** = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e81fa4ffa839030990b565a712b8ed84f6fab03ce5beec1c1c5b24ae48083a3c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 4 × (17)²

⇒ We know, (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂

⇒ (46)² = 1156 + 2d₁d₂

⇒ 2116 = 1156 + 2d₁d₂

⇒ 2d₁d₂ = 2116 − 1156 = 960

⇒ d₁d₂ = 480

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 480 = 240 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 240 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides of a **rhombus** are equal, and the **diagonals** bisect each other at 90° (perpendicularly).

Diagonal and Side Relation

The relation between the side 'a' and diagonals d₁, d₂ is given by 4a² = d₁² + d₂², which is derived from the **Pythagoras theorem**.

Area Formulas

Area of a **rhombus** = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂ OR Area = Base × Height.

questions.question: R alone can do a work in 18 days. P alone can do the same work in 24 days. G alone can do the same work in 36 days. They started and completed the work together. They received Rs. 7200 for this work. What is the share (in Rs.) of P?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Efficiency** is the reciprocal of **Time** taken: 1/18 : 1/24 : 1/36.

Multiply by **LCM (72)** to get the ratio: 4 : 3 : 2.

Total efficiency parts = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 parts.

**P's share** = (Efficiency of P ÷ Total Efficiency) × Total Wage.

**P's share** = (3 ÷ 9) × 7200 = 1/3 × 7200 = ₹2400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time taken by **G** = 36 days

Total amount received = **₹7200**

**Formula Used:**

When multiple people work for the same amount of time, their **Wages** are distributed in the ratio of their **Efficiencies**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of **Efficiency** (R : P : G) = 4 : 3 : 2

⇒ Sum of **Efficiency** ratios = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 units

⇒ 9 units = ₹7200

⇒ 1 unit = 7200 ÷ 9 = ₹800

⇒ **P's share** (3 units) = 3 × 800

⇒ **P's share** = ₹2400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Relationship

questions.question: A car travels three equal distances at the speed of 10 km/hr, 30 km/hr and 60 km/hr respectively. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for this journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume each equal **distance** is the **LCM** of speeds (10, 30, 60) = 60 km.

**Total Distance** = 3 × 60 = 180 km.

**Total Time** = (60 ÷ 10) + (60 ÷ 30) + (60 ÷ 60) = 6 + 2 + 1 = 9 hours.

**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time** = 180 ÷ 9 = 20 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Speeds** of three equal parts of the journey are 10 km/hr, 30 km/hr, and 60 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** **Average Speed** = (3 × v₁ × v₂ × v₃) ÷ (v₁v₂ + v₂v₃ + v₃v₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e47fd8b7013bc572c211864df7a3d3f26aa8a29a15534dcf125dd262cb5228a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three equal **distances** be **d** each.

⇒ Total **Distance** = d + d + d = 3d

⇒ Total **Time** = (d ÷ 10) + (d ÷ 30) + (d ÷ 60)

⇒ Total **Time** = (6d + 2d + d) ÷ 60 = 9d ÷ 60 = 3d ÷ 20

⇒ **Average Speed** = (3d) ÷ (3d ÷ 20)

⇒ **Average Speed** = 3d × (20 ÷ 3d) = 20 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, the **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert **Speed** from km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Constant Time Case

If a person travels for equal **intervals of time** at different speeds v₁ and v₂, the **Average Speed** is simply the arithmetic mean: (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2.

⇒ **SP** = 100x × 4 = 400x

⇒ Discount = **MP** − **SP** = 450x − 400x = 50x

⇒ **Discount %** = (50x ÷ 450x) × 100

⇒ **Discount %** = (1 ÷ 9) × 100 = 11.111...

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11 percent.**

Mark-up Percentage

Profit and Discount Relation

Will the infrastructure projects have been completed by the government before the deadline set by the council?

options.text: Will the government complete the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will the government have completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will have the government completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will the government completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the government have completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Perfect Tense**, indicated by the construction **will + object + have been + past participle (completed)**.
 
• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice in the **Future Perfect Tense**, the structure must follow: **Will + Subject + have + Past Participle (V3) + Object?**
 
• In the passive sentence, **the government** is the agent (doer), and **the infrastructure projects** is the patient (receiver). In the active voice, **the government** shifts to the **subject** position.
 
• The auxiliary verb **will** remains at the start to maintain the **interrogative form**, followed immediately by the new subject.
 
• The phrase **before the deadline set by the council** is an **adverbial modifier** that provides temporal context and remains unchanged in its position at the end of the sentence.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Perfect Tense**:
 
 
• It denotes an action that will be **completed** between now and a specific point in the future.
 
• In **Active Voice**, the helping verbs are **will have** followed by the **third form of the verb**.
 
 
 
• **Common Structural Errors**:
 
 
• **Future Simple**: Using **will complete** (as seen in Option 1) changes the aspect of the verb from perfect to simple.
 
• **Syntax Errors**: Placing the auxiliary **have** before the subject (as in Option 3) creates an **incorrect interrogative structure** in English.
 
• **Morphological Errors**: Using **will** directly with **completed** (as in Option 4) without **have** is grammatically invalid.
 
 
</ul

Each of the representatives from the various states have presented their reports on healthcare reforms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary grammatical issue in the sentence is the **Subject-Verb Agreement**.
 
• The subject of the sentence is '**Each**', which is a **singular distributive pronoun**.
 
• In English grammar, when '**Each of**' is followed by a plural noun (in this case, 'representatives'), the **verb** must always remain **singular**.
 
• The original sentence incorrectly uses the plural verb '**have presented**'. To make it grammatically correct, it must be replaced by the singular verb '**has presented**'.
 
• While traditional grammar often preferred 'his or her' with 'each', modern usage commonly accepts '**their**' as a singular gender-neutral pronoun, making **Option 2** the most suitable choice among the given alternatives.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Each of the representatives from the various states **has presented their reports** on healthcare reforms.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** '**have presented their report**' – This is incorrect because it retains the plural verb '**have**'.
 
• **Option 3:** '**were presented their reports**' – This is incorrect because '**were**' is a plural verb and the passive construction changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** '**No improvement required**' – This is incorrect because the original sentence contains a clear **subject-verb agreement error** where a plural verb is used for a singular subject.

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
She didn't study for the test, so she was unable to answer most of the questions.

options.text: She didn't studied for the test
She don't study for the test
She doesn't study for the test

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part of the sentence is **grammatically correct** and does not require any changes.
 
• The sentence is set in the **past tense**, as indicated by the phrase **was unable** in the second clause.
 
• In the **simple past tense** (negative), the structure used is **subject + did not (didn't) + base form of the verb**.
 
• The phrase **didn't study** correctly follows this rule, where **didn't** is the auxiliary verb and **study** is the base form (V1).
 
• Therefore, the sentence is **consistent in tense** and logically sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is **No improvement required**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'She **didn't study for the test**, so she was unable to answer most of the questions.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** 'She **didn't studied**' is incorrect because the auxiliary verb **did** is already in the past tense; the main verb must remain in its **base form**.
 
• **Option 2:** 'She **don't study**' is incorrect because **don't** is used with plural subjects (and I/you), while **She** is third-person singular. Furthermore, it is in the **present tense**.
 
• **Option 3:** 'She **doesn't study**' is grammatically correct as a standalone phrase in the **present tense**, but it creates a **tense mismatch** with the rest of the sentence (was unable).
</ul
